steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A logo must work at ALL scales — from a billboard to a favicon; simplicity and clarity are key.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Brand guidelines document: logo usage rules, colour palette (Pantone, CMYK, RGB), typography, imagery style, spacing requirements.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Consistency across all applications builds recognition — stationery, packaging, digital, signage must all speak the same visual language.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Rebranding involves updating an existing identity — it must balance familiarity with freshness.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring branding and corporate identity. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with branding and corporate identity. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with branding and corporate identity. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to branding and corporate identity, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined  | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
